svg.text: Modular monolith on Kubernetes: API (synchronous) + Worker (asynchronous) over PostgreSQL, Redis and Kafka. Every arrow is labelled; double-headed = request/response or read/write, single-headed = one-way push.
Transaction API — ASP.NET Core 10 minimal APIs
K8s Deployment · HPA · PDB · :8080 · metrics :9464 · no background services
forwarded headers → request-context logging (correlation id) → exception handler (RFC 7807 ProblemDetails) → security headers
→ Prometheus http metrics → HSTS / HTTPS → compression → CORS → auth-failure throttle (Redis) → JWT authentication → role policies (staff | admin)
→ Redis fixed-window rate limiter (global 200/min, API group 150/min) → endpoint filters (API-key, view-audit) → MediatR: validation → logging → caching
Composition shared with the Worker: TransactionAggregation.Hosting + BuildingBlocks
MediatR behaviours · Result → ProblemDetails · IUserContext / InstitutionAccess · AccountFilter · IModuleMigration registry · IDevelopmentSeeder · outbox/inbox building block
What the API does and does not do
Synchronous path touches only PostgreSQL (via PgBouncer), Redis and Keycloak. Anything slow or external — Kafka, bank alert
webhooks, rebuilding aggregates — is done by the Worker, handed over through the Inbox/Outbox tables, so a slow bank or a broker
outage never blocks a request. A webhook delivery is stored (idempotent on its id) and acknowledged with 202 Accepted.
Transaction Worker — all background processing, and only here
K8s Deployment, scales independently of the API · :8080 health · metrics :9464 · organised by module
Hosting + BuildingBlocks · BackgroundUserContext (no signed-in user: user-initiated operations belong to the API)
Inbox/Outbox rows are claimed with a lease and retried with backoff; poison messages are dead-lettered; handlers are idempotent,
so everything is at-least-once with exactly-once effect on the ledger (unique per bank + external id, re-delivery is detected).
Runs before every rollout, as the schema owner tagg_migrator

In-process module collaboration: compile-time dependencies, only through *.Contracts (enforced by architecture tests)
IAuditTrail.RecordWithin (same DB transaction as the ledger write)
Each module = Domain · Application · Infrastructure · Presentation (+ Contracts). No module touches another module's Domain, Application or Infrastructure.
Key flows (numbered on the diagram) and design decisions
Bank → Traefik → API: the API key resolves the bank (WebhookSources), the payload is validated, an InboxMessage is stored (idempotent on Idempotency-
Key) with its audit event, and the API answers 202. The Worker's inbox dispatcher claims it, normalizes and categorizes, then writes the ledger rows,
a TransactionRecorded outbox event and the audit trail in one transaction. The outbox dispatcher publishes the event to transaction-events and clears
A signed record on bank-transactions: the Worker verifies the HMAC and the bank, then follows the same inbox path as (1). Unauthenticated or poison
records go to bank-transactions.dlq. Offsets are committed only after the hand-off to the inbox.
Browser → Traefik → API: JWT and role policy, rate limiter, Redis cache, then the query. Lists are live from the ledger with keyset paging; aggregates
come only from reporting.DailyTotals and carry asOf.
Worker job every N minutes: advisory lock, recompute whole account-days touched since the watermark (South African calendar days), replace those rows
in reporting.DailyTotals, move the checkpoint, invalidate the aggregates cache.
Processing detects a re-delivered or duplicated entry, writes an outbox event, the Notifications handler POSTs to the bank's registered alert URL
(https, public host only, URL stored encrypted).
CI builds the images, the db-migrate Job applies the ordered migrations as tagg_migrator under an advisory lock, then API and Worker roll out
connecting as tagg_app with secrets from Vault or k8s Secrets.
Modular monolith, two deployables: seven modules (own DbContext and schema, joined only by *.Contracts) in one
codebase; the API and the Worker scale independently.
Transactional Inbox/Outbox: at-least-once delivery with idempotent handlers; the ledger write, the outbox event
and the audit row commit atomically.
CQRS read model: aggregates are never computed on a request. The Worker rebuilds reporting.DailyTotals and every
response states how fresh it is (asOf).
Multi-currency: the ledger keeps the native currency; conversion happens at read time from one catalog
Least privilege and defence in depth: separate migrator and app DB roles, append-only audit, JWT roles, per-bank
API keys, HMAC-signed Kafka, rate limits, SSRF-safe alert URLs.
Operability: Serilog to Seq, OpenTelemetry traces, prometheus-net metrics, dashboards as code, health probes on
both deployables, PDB and HPA on the API.
Fail-safe boundaries: a slow bank, a broker outage or a bad payload never blocks a request; work is durable in
Postgres and retried by the Worker.
